how_to_read: entities: new entities in the strokes format, ready to copy into a part (as S4's merge_fixes accept()). retire: entities to drop in merge_fixes.mjs, with the reason. changes: edits to existing entities; 'set' keys are fields or 'pts.<name>' points, 'members_remove'/'members_add' edit a group, 'add_note' is text to append to the note. checked: the merge notes' list for this range (and other low entities), read again, with the verdict and the reading. Crops are in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ran-3d-director/5a5a3bca-3a69-416d-986a-71fd47398c96/scratchpad/S2_second_middle/ (c_* colour, n_* colour normalised, g_* greyscale contrast-stretched, i_* scan beside the canal/west restyle, ov* overlays of map/strokes/S2.json); crop.mjs there makes them (node crop.mjs u0 u1 v0 v1 zoom out [c|n|g] [tick]).

A very long, high-sided boat lying along the north bank, bow west, close beside 逆水行舟 to its south and end to end with 豪华客船 to its west: at the bow (u 23700-23900) a curved arched beam over a dark mat hood, a deck post and a spoked windlass; on deck a flat board platform on legs and big round coils of rope or baskets (23940-24090, v 635-725) and a short ladder leaning from the deck up to the bank (top at (24045, 505)); amidships a flat mat-roofed deckhouse open at the sides (roof u 24275-24583, v 496-530) with a second arched beam and a dark mat hood at its east end (24425-24600, v 586-730); east of it a spoked wheel or windlass on a post (24640-24740, v 523-590); aft a huge rounded mat cover over the cargo, topped with a woven round basket (24775-25137, v 542-667); a high curved stern with a carved post and the rudder stock at u ~25100-25130. A coil or round fender hangs on its south side at (24380, 840), and at the bow a long rope-wrapped fender (or bundle) hangs on a line over its south side, between it and 逆水行舟's foredeck (u 23735-23768, v 745-872). No mast. Its many strakes with rivet rows show it riding high (unladen). Crew: a man at the bow (the spoked windlass beside him is unmanned), one or two men at the aft windlass, two crouching on deck, two in the deckhouse and a man poling at the gunwale.

lessons: A hung fender or a scroll-ended bitt looks like a standing crewman at the scan's resolution: a head-sized top over a body-sized column. Before keeping a faint crewman, compare its head's width with a certain figure's head on the same deck (S2: 35 px against the poler's 20), and look at the column's lines: a robe has vertical folds and arms, a rope-wrapped fender has close horizontal wrappings and tapers to its foot.

Settle seated or standing by painted height against standing neighbours at a similar foot v, not by the furniture beside the figure: S2's eatery man is 72 px at v 398 where standing men are 92-109 px at v 301-373, so he sits on the bench, though a 40 px table stands next to him.

Windlasses, cranks and spoked wheels are the commonest false crew on S2's boats: their end discs read as bent backs and their spoke ends as heads. A head on this scan is a 15-25 px dark mass (hair or cap) or a closed double outline; a 3-8 px stroke rising to a point is a spoke or post top.
